transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I go from feeling like I can work nonstop and take on everything to suddenly having no energy to even show up for my shifts. It's been making things really difficult for me at the restaurant lately, and my manager is starting to notice.
During those times when you have high energy and take on everything, do you find that you need much less sleep than usual or that you feel unusually talkative or impulsive?

Yeah, during those high periods, I feel like I don't need rest at all and will stay up all night sketching business plans. I also talk constantly and so fast that people can't get a word in, while impulsively taking on way too many shifts and projects.

During these high-energy periods, have you ever felt so out of control or reckless that you required hospitalization, or did these episodes ever lead to significant problems that caused you to lose your job or get into serious trouble?

No, I've never been hospitalized during those times. I haven't lost my job, but I have been written up for no-shows and mistakes, which is putting my employment at risk, and I've also fallen behind on my rent and bills.
Have you experienced these cycles of high energy and low energy for at least two years, or are these distinct episodes separated by periods where you feel completely like yourself?

No, this hasn't been going on for two years at all. The whole cycle of highs and lows actually started about four months ago when I began taking on all those extra double shifts at work. The intense high period lasted for a few weeks, but I've been stuck in this heavy, low stretch now for about the last three months.
During those high-energy periods, did your symptoms last for at least one full week, or were they shorter in duration?

Yes, they definitely lasted longer than a week. That high-energy period went on for about a full month before I crashed. It was a solid few weeks of feeling like I could do absolutely everything without stopping.
During those high-energy periods, did you experience any symptoms like hearing voices, seeing things that weren't there, or feeling like you had special powers or abilities?

No, I didn't hear voices or see things that weren't there, but I did have this overwhelming feeling that I was capable of absolutely anything. I was completely convinced I could easily launch a food truck and run my own restaurant chain in a year, and I even talked to my manager like I knew more than him despite dropping out of college.

During those high-energy periods, did your behavior become so disruptive or extreme that it caused a marked impairment in your social or occupational functioning, or did you ever have to be hospitalized to prevent harm to yourself or others?

I've never been hospitalized, but my behavior definitely caused a lot of disruption in my life. I became so overwhelming that my friends started avoiding me, and I made careless mistakes at work that got me written up and put my job at risk.

During those high-energy periods, did your behavior become so extreme that it was clearly noticeable to others as a major change in your personality, or was it something that could still be seen as a 'boost' in your usual productivity?

It was definitely a major, noticeable change rather than just a productivity boost. My mother got really concerned about my sudden change in energy, and my manager even pulled me aside to talk about my erratic behavior. Plus, my friends found me way too wired and overwhelming to be around during those times.
During the three months you've been feeling low, have you experienced symptoms like a complete loss of interest in all activities, significant weight changes, or thoughts of death or suicide?

Yeah, I've completely stopped playing Sunday soccer and cooking new recipes, and now I just sit around scrolling on my phone because everything feels pointless. My appetite is also all over the place—I'll forget to eat all day or inhale a whole pizza at midnight, so my clothes are starting to hang off me, but I haven't had any thoughts of death or suicide.
